codebook_ambiguities: admitted vs evidence_only: in this code version EVIDENCE_ONLY spans create evidence (memory_gatekeeper_service._build_gate_decision) and extract_for_project extracts every evidence span, so evidence_only spans do get claims. The admitted step (extract_to_state/extract_as_candidate, or a carrier from ANOTHER span) does not say what happens when the carrier comes from an evidence_only cited span (a0_r2 F10).

Re-extraction: extract_from_evidence is idempotent only when claims already exist, so evidence whose extraction returned zero claims is extracted again in later phases (a0_r2 F69: EL2020c span, 0 claims at ph2, claim produced at ph3). 'Extracted by checkpoint k' must use the extraction step's phase, not the evidence's meeting.

current-step sub-code: the codebook does not say whether it is decided by the immediate successor that broke the fact's currency or by the fact current at k. In a0_r1 F06 the successor '5 languages' is non-gold, but the fact current at k=3, 'as multilingual as possible', is F66's gold alias.

displaced_by_other_gold_value vs overwritten_by_non_gold_value when the displacing value is another row's gold value filed under the wrong key (a0_r2 F10, displaced by F85's value). The value-based rule says 'displaced'; the Limits section frames misrouting as 'overwritten'.

Several single-value questions at one checkpoint (a0_r1 F82: cs_F82 resolved other keys, yesno_F82 resolved the right key and got the fact). The codebook does not say whether key_reached, in_payload and answered aggregate over any asking question or use a specific one.

codebook_ambiguities: Compound gold values (F03, F05, F64, F88, F32, F22) are often split by extraction into several claims on different keys, each holding one part (often exactly a gold alias). The codebook does not say whether a claim or fact holding only one part 'carries the value'. I accepted partial carriers that match a gold alias; a stricter coder would move these rows earlier (to carried) or later (to answered).

Ruled-out rows: the chain says 'as current', so modality must be asserted. But rejections are often voiced as a tentative question that the next speaker confirms (R03: 'we should not use the Antrecorp test sets, right?' / 'Yes, exactly'), and the confirmation lands in the next gatekeeper span. The codebook has no rule for a confirmation in an adjacent span or for negative-proposed carriers.

Values that contain their own negation (F30 'not much better than before'; A1 F64 'TSV files ... as not the end of the workflow') are tagged negative by extraction and stored as REJECTED facts. The polarity step codes this as carried_only_negative, the same code as a real ruling-out; the codebook does not separate double negation from rejection.

credit_without_state is defined for rows 'lost before reading'. A1 F59 was lost at key_reached, a reading step, and was still scored correct from citation text with the fact never in the payload. It is unclear whether the flag covers rows lost inside reading (key_reached/in_payload).

in_payload counts near matches as given, but the answer composer appears to ignore near matches. In a0_r3 F03 the fact was a current_confirmed near match and the reader abstained. Such losses land in answered/answer_or_judge although the fact was never among the reader's facts.

Matcher bounds vs semantic judgement: the codebook counts a one-word-alias match only from the cited span. A human coder may judge an other-span text such as 'contacting people / validators' (F64 in both runs) to be the same value. The task asks for semantic judgement, so the bound and the instruction can disagree.

Choosing the cited span: cited lines can straddle two gatekeeper spans (R03: line 124 in one span, lines 125/127 in the next). Short lines ('Yes, exactly.', 'Yeah, yeah.') recur verbatim in other spans, and spans merge consecutive turns of one speaker, so matching a line with its speaker prefix fails. The codebook does not define how 'the cited span' is located.

overwritten_by_non_gold_value vs displaced_by_other_gold_value: the codebook does not say whether to judge the immediate successor or the value current at k when a value is overwritten more than once (a0_r3 F24: two successors, both non-gold, so no conflict here).

State timestamps are not transaction time. In A0, valid_from/valid_to are the ingestion time of the meeting cited by the claim's evidence; in A1 they are meeting dates (repair_meeting_dates). Creation phase must come from the trace's proposal phase. The codebook says so only through its matching rule (key, value, type, in order).

In A1, settle-before-confirm gives two resolution passes per phase. 'Last evaluation by k' must mean the settle pass, and a first-pass proposal can expire. The codebook does not mention this; it did not change any row sampled here.

The 'rejection' family includes multi-value 'rejected_so_far' questions (5-8 values) as well as single-value 'rej_Rxx' questions. The codebook lists 'rejection' as single-value and does not say whether rejected_so_far questions count for reading.

findings.claim: conflict_service.evaluate_claim returns without a conflict_detection log in several cases: 'Claim has no state key; skipped.'; 'Design cycle 2: claim parked (...)'; the two D9 'span does not establish ...' parks; 'Stage-23 repair (bug 1): this ruling-out is already recorded.'. _c2_reroute logs under seam filing_type_check instead. Consequences: (a) the 'Claim has no state key' prefix in filing() and the trail path to 'cycle2_parked' can never match; parked claims with an earlier logged row are coded 'filed' (A2). (b) ('Stage-23 repair (bug 1)', 'ruling_out_already_recorded') can never see its intended noop. The only logged reason with that prefix is the engine supersede 'Stage-23 repair (bug 1): current value ruled out; ...', which carries a proposal and should be another_value_won. status_at's startswith('Only hedged') also misreads 'Stage-23 repair (bug 1): current value ruled out; Only hedged...' as confirmed. Map 'Stage-23 repair (bug 1): current value ruled out' to another_value_won, or test result_type/proposal_id before the reason prefixes. findings.title: applied_after_checkpoint is reported when the by-k proposal expired and a different, later proposal applied the value
findings.claim: Under the structural policy, a proposal raised by k is applied in its own phase, expires at the bug-13 settle, or stays pending forever. 'applied_after_checkpoint' therefore never means 'applied late'; here the proposal that passed 'proposed' expired. Reproducing rows: a1_r1 F06 k=0 (proposal cf7623, phase 0, new, status expired; fact cb70c621 '42 languages' created in phase 1 by another proposal) and a1_r3 F06 k=0 (941642 expired; facts 5d2e558c and 179dbe63 created in phase 1). Both are coded applied:applied_after_checkpoint. The proposal-level outcome is proposal_expired.

findings.title: Fact-to-proposal placement prefers type over transaction order; an exact creation-order join exists
findings.claim: Facts are sorted by valid_from. Each takes the first unused proposal of type 'supersede' if it has a predecessor, otherwise 'new'. In A0, valid_from is the winning claim's ingestion time, so ties are common. A 'new' proposal applied while another fact was current supersedes it, which breaks the type rule. Reproducing case: a0_r3 key project.adoble_slt_test_set.owner. Fact c682d784 'PERSON2' is placed in phase 2 (supersede 22f4b420) and 54ed3822 'PERSON2' in phase 0 (new 0012a560); creation order gives 0 and 2. This produces supersession-chain inversions, and it is the 6209/6210 mismatch the codebook reports. Check: the dump's proposals align 1:1, in order, with the script's first-seen pids in all six runs, and the accepted proposals align 1:1 with state_facts in dump order (a1_r2 skips one in-place demotion). That merge reproduces every other placement exactly. Commands: <W>/place_cmp.py <W> and <W>/place_rows.py <W>.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 2 facts; 0 gold rows change outcome in these runs
findings.suggested_fix: Place facts by merging dump state_facts (creation order) with dump proposals whose status is accepted (also creation order, aligned to trace pids), or at least enforce created[successor] >= created[predecessor]. This also prevents an expired proposal from being matched to a fact.

findings.title: Demoted-fact rejection phase ignores creation time
findings.claim: _rejection_phase takes the minimum phase over every reject proposal with the same key and exact value, including one raised before the fact existed. rejected_at for a demoted fact also skips the c<=k check. Under A1 (open_only), the following can happen: value V gets a ruled-out record in phase 0, is adopted in phase 1 as fact F, and is demoted in phase 2 by a new reject pid. F would then read not current at k=1 and 'rejected' at k=0. Only one demoted-in-place fact exists in the six runs (a1_r2 39a138fb 'very unstable', created 0, reject phase 3), and it is handled correctly. The value match is exact, but projection matches strip().lower().
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 0 in these runs (latent)
findings.suggested_fix: Use the minimum phase of reject proposals with phase >= created[fid], add c<=k in rejected_at, and compare values with strip().lower() as the projection does.

findings.title: Latent collection-key and hidden-reject joins
findings.claim: (1) Collection path, _evaluate_collection_claim: a reject-membership proposal is logged with result_type 'new'. The script records its type as 'new', so it counts as 'proposed' for a current row, is missed for a ruled_out row, and the resulting REJECTED member cannot be placed. The collection value is also taken raw from object.value, while the app proposes canon=to_canonical(value or role).strip(). (2) _dispatch with the bug-1 repair calls _repair_reject_ruled_out, which creates a reject proposal for the current value. That proposal's id never appears in any trace row, because the row carries only the supersede pid. The script never sees it, and its REJECTED fact would be unplaced. All 177 definitions and 196 expansion proposals in these runs are scalar, and no bug-1 reasons appear, so nothing fires here; proposals_without_value and facts_not_placed_in_time are 0.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: 0 in these runs (latent; first collection key or bug-1 supersede would mis-code)
findings.suggested_fix: For cardinality == 'collection', set type='reject' when the reason starts with 'Rejected-membership' or 'Ruled-out value recorded as rejected-member', and canonicalise like the app. Raise a hard error when a dump proposal or fact cannot be joined, instead of only counting it.

findings.title: credit_without_state misses rows lost at reading that are scored correct
findings.claim: credit_without_state returns False for any reading-boundary loss. A row lost at key_reached, where the reader never resolved a key holding the fact, but whose asking question is scored correct, carries no flag. That is the same 'credit without the traced state' situation. Counts: a0_r2, a0_r3 and a1_r1 each have 1 such row at the lower bound (3 total).
findings.suggested_fix: Flag (or count separately) rows whose loss is key_reached or in_payload but whose asked question is correct.

findings.title: Codebook text does not match the code in several places
findings.claim: (a) The filed row says 'last evaluation by k was under a defined key'. In A0, undefined-key claims are coded 'filed' (only the bug-5 repair reason gives undefined_key); flag bug5 marks them. (b) 'Defect flags ... taken from the facts that carry the value': flags are computed only for rows that reach 'applied'. At an applied failure they come from facts created after k, or ruled-out records. 28 A0 rows lost at extraction or filing have strong value-carrying facts that would be flagged, but carry none. (c) 'An adjudication made by a model is labelled as non-human': the code records only the path and sha256; there is no adjudicator field. (d) proposal_<status> reads end-of-run statuses of all dump proposals on the key, reject proposals included, not the status of the props that passed 'proposed'. (e) Phase = number of checkpoints already questioned, so a checkpoint without questions would shift all later phases; harmless for EL2020 (20/25/30/30 questions).
findings.estimated_rows_affected: documentation only (b: 28 A0 rows' flags)
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the filed and flag definitions, add an adjudicator field (human/model) to the adjudication YAML schema and output, and derive phase from per-meeting ingest boundaries or assert that every checkpoint has questions.

findings.title: Strong matches count from any span, so short values and generic aliases pick up unrelated claims and facts
findings.location: 23-loss-trace.py match_level() lines 192-216 and trace_row() carries() lines 510-517 (the locality test is applied only when lv == 'weak'); codebook 23-loss-trace.md, Matcher/Bounds
findings.claim: Locality is enforced for weak matches only. A strong match from any span, or from any fact, decides carried, proposed, applied and current. I judged all 385 strong (fact_id, text) pairs that decided a lower-bound pass across the six runs. Wrong-fact or false texts (X+F) are 18/239 (7.5%) of the pairs local to the cited span, but 106/146 (72.6%) of the non-local ones. Examples, all strong: a0_r1 F21 'Czech and English' k=2 is carried by 'English to Czech' (EL2020d#17, a translation direction) and 'Czech speech translated into English' (EL2020a#3, thesis data). a0_r1 F21 k=2 gets lower bound ok:stored_not_asked; with the false texts removed it becomes proposed:another_value_won. a1_r2 F58 k=3 is carried by 'GitHub issue tracker for cruise control' through alias 'cruise control' (ok:stored_not_asked -> current:rejected). a1_r1 F61 k=2 is carried by 'trained on several other data sets' through alias 'training data'. a0_r3 F61 k=3 is carried by 'only dev set has been evaluated so far; test set has not yet been processed' through alias 'not to the test set'.
findings.estimated_rows_affected: Overriding the 73 F texts changes (loss, sub) on 54/954 row-runs (5.7%). Overriding the F+X texts changes 87/954 (9.1%). Lower-bound passes that rest only on F/X texts: carried 15/702, applied 46/491 (9.4%), ok 19/212 (9.0%). Generic-phrase class alone: 43 row-runs (F21 14, F61 7, F25 5, F84 3, F39 3, F24 3, F58 3, F27 2, F92 1, F86 1, R07 1).
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the locality rule to strong matches too. Treat a non-local strong text like a weak one: it counts only in the upper bound and goes to the adjudication queue. Widen 'local' to the cited span ±1 in the same meeting. Measured against the semantic reference (lower bound with judged F/X texts overridden), agreement rises from 867/954 to 898/954 with locality alone and to 902/954 with the ±1 window. The remaining disagreements are true restatements in other meetings (F06 '42 languages' at EL2020b#22, F11 'Every Tuesday' at EL2020b#1, F26 at EL2020c#23), which the adjudication queue then settles.

findings.title: Gold aliases shared between sibling rows: a demoted value is scored still_current when its gold successor is stored
findings.location: suite gold block (transfer_el2020.yaml: F36 aliases 'pause duration(s)' vs F59; F38 alias '42 languages' = F06 value; F06/F38 alias '42'; F58 alias 'cruise control'/'simple script' vs F24/F37/F25; F61 vs R04 'not to the test set'; R05 'TPU only' vs F70; R08 'separate paper' vs F91); trace_row demoted branch lines 530-540

Demoted F36 (silence duration, rejected at k=2) is carried by F59's stored value 'based on pause durations' (alias 'pause durations'). So F36 becomes current:still_current exactly when the system correctly stored its successor, e.g. a0_r1 F36 k=2 and k=3 ('working on Czech segmentor based on pause durations', key project.assessment.czech_segmenter_quality).
